# 7.2 · Agent Loop

`Level 7: Agents Without Magic` · `+35 XP` · `drill 2 of 3`

## The job
Write `run_agent(model, registry, user_message, max_steps, system)`. Start the transcript
with an optional system message and the user message. Each step, call `model(messages)`:
a `final` reply ends the run; a `tool_call` reply is recorded, run through
`registry.call`, and its result appended as a `tool` message; anything else gets a system
message explaining the valid reply shapes. Stop after `max_steps` model calls. Return
`{"answer", "steps", "stopped", "messages", "tool_calls"}`.

## Why it matters
This loop is what every agent framework wraps. Getting the transcript right is the whole
game: the model only knows what you put back into the messages, so a tool error that never
makes it into the transcript is a mistake the model can never fix. The step limit is the
seatbelt that keeps a confused model from looping until the bill arrives.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 7.2     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 7.2      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Message shapes: user {"role": "user", "content": text}; tool request {"role": "assistant", "tool_call": {"name", "args"}}; tool result {"role": "tool", "name", "content": the dict from registry.call}; final {"role": "assistant", "content": text}.
2. `tool_calls` in the result is a list of (name, ok) pairs, one per tool call, in order.
3. `stopped` is "final" when the model answered and "max_steps" when you cut it off (then answer is None).
4. An invalid reply still counts as a step. Append {"role": "system", "content": ...} that names the two valid reply types.
5. `kit.tools.ToolRegistry` is the registry; `kit.fakemodel.ScriptedModel` is what the tests use as a model.

</details>
